title: Priority customer bridge: streaming timeout multiplexer and idempotent replay safety
creator: Sana Patel
description:
Summary:
A high-severity customer escalation reported repeated intermittent 5xx/timeouts during long streaming requests (tokenized chat) that surface only under moderate tenant-concurrency. Investigation shows a streaming multiplexer race in the fronting proxy + backend hedging producing head-of-line blocking and amplified client retries.

Observed behavior:
- Tenant A issues long-lived streaming chat sessions while Tenant B spikes; system begins to coalesce streams on shared front-door worker causing a per-worker request queue to grow.
- When a backend token-generation worker enters a slowpath (KV-sync stall), downstream multiplexer stalls other tenant streams; clients hit SDK-side retry logic and produce replay storms.
- Symptoms: 502/504 and timeouts, inflated retry_count in telemetry, increased request amplification for affected tenant leading to cascading 5xx wave.

Cross-environment note:
- Hosted: more visible due to front-door multiplexing across many tenants and autoscaling cold-start sensitivity.
- Dedicated: observed but attenuated (reserved capacity reduces admission stacking).
- Private: potential for reproduction on on-prem where multiplexer settings haven't been tuned.

Root cause hypothesis:
- The streaming multiplexer's per-worker FIFO combined with a synchronous KV cache compaction path allowed a single slow request to block other multiplexed streams. Recovery logic in the proxy delayed finishing the client connection, producing idempotent-replay collisions when retries re-entered the system.

Proposed short-term mitigation (hotfix):
1) Implement per-tenant admission cap at the fronting multiplexer (soft limit) to prevent one slow stream from monopolizing worker queues.
2) Fast-fail hedging backend requests earlier when backend latency exceeds threshold (reduce retry amplification).
3) Add an idempotency token check in the multiplexer that deduplicates immediate client replay within a 10s window.

Proposed medium-term fixes:
- Rework multiplexer to allow fair-queueing per-tenant and preemptive drain of stalled stream slots.
- Move KV compaction off critical path or make it async with backpressure tokens.
- Enhance SDK guidance: reduce default aggressive retry policy for streaming calls and surface clear retry headers to the server.

Telemetry & dashboards to add before rollout:
- tenant_retry_count (per-minute), streaming_head_of_line_duration, backend_kv_sync_stall_count, multiplexer_queue_depth_by_worker, idempotent_replay_hits.
- New Grafana panel: tenant-impact heatmap correlating spikes to 5xx surge windows.

Rollout plan:
- Canary (hosted): 1% tenants -> 2 hours stability check -> 10% -> 24h -> 100% if no spike in 5xx or head-of-line metrics.
- Dedicated: opt-in patch for tenant clusters, recommend immediate patch for clusters with >10 concurrent streams per-GPU.
- Private: publish advisory and patch bundle; offer assisted upgrade for enterprise customers with escalations.

Rollback criteria:
- Increase in client-observed streaming errors > 0.5% relative to baseline, or increased tail latency for non-impacted tenants, or idempotent-replay false positives > 0.1%.

Testing plan:
- Synthetic load harness that reproduces long-stream + burst tenant interplay (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/stream-sim, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/stream-sim/pull/112).
- Unit tests for idempotency window and multiplexer admission caps.
- End-to-end regression job in CI that simulates KV compaction pauses.

Customer comms:
- Notify impacted customer with preliminary mitigations and ETA for hotfix (internal bridge ID #CB-2025-17).
- Prepare status page blurb and targeted email if canary shows improvement.

Artifacts & links:
- Incident timeline & notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/CB-2025-17-streaming-escalation
- Telemetry dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streaming/tenant-impact
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6298
- Simulation harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/stream-sim/pull/112

Acceptance criteria:
- No recurring tenant-level 5xx waves for 7 days post-rollout in hosted region-us-west1.
- Multiplexer queue depth reduced by >= 60% for simulated long-stream scenario.
- Idempotent-replay hits are stable and deduplications exceed 90% for retries within 10s window.
